goal: Hook: a note typed on one classroom device turns up on another, and the class meets the compelling question; then students act the parts of a computer (input, processor, memory and storage, output) as a key press becomes a letter, and trace typing and saving a note through the four-part system-diagram, saying which part is hardware, which is software and where the note is kept when the device is off.
note: Unplugged first (role cards, the system-diagram mat), then device in part: the note typed and saved on any school device with a plain note tool, about 10 minutes. A classroom thermometer reading named as another input. Retrieval inside the session after the hook (no opening trace on session 1): name the part a staged fault sits in on the system-diagram (g4-troubleshoot). Paths: one device per pair; a few devices at stations with the other pairs on the paper version; one screen with a student at the keys for each step; no device. No student is asked what devices are at home. Devices carried with two hands, cords behind the table.

goal: The parts of a wired and a wireless network (device, cable, switch, router, access point, modem) labeled on a network-diagram with each one's job; the class acts the parts with yarn, traces the day 1 note to another device, then sorts the part cards into wired, wireless or both.
note: Opens with the three-minute retrieval trace. Retrieval: say one way a cable and one way wireless is better (g4-wired-wireless), and the day 1 note traced through the system-diagram. Unplugged. Yarn lies on the floor, never stretched at ankle height; students walk. No real school network is examined and no student is asked about the network at home. Out: no addresses, packets or protocols (grade 6).

goal: The cia-triangle, one story a side (a locked diary, a note changed on the way or a photo that may not be real, a library closed when you need a book); students match new threats to the side they hurt, say why that side matters, then decide what to keep private and why, and keep a pretend password private on a paper account.
note: Opens with the three-minute retrieval trace. Retrieval: sort two cards, proving who you are versus what you may open (g4-authn-authz), and the network part where a message can be read, changed or blocked. Sensitive: passwords and personal information. No real password, address or name is said or written; every account is paper and pretend; the teacher page carries health's "If a student tells you something" steps word for word. Unplugged. Base: archived Year 6 Communication and collaboration lesson 6 (what to share, then why: the Candidate order, kept at zero days), moved ahead to sit with the triangle; the base is not yet loaded (later.csv L149).

goal: End-of-unit assessment, a written paper of about 25 minutes with unseen items: label a new system-diagram and trace a new task through it, naming for each of input, processing, storage and output the hardware part and the software doing it; sort new network part cards and give each one's job; match four new threats to the triangle's sides, at least one threat for each side, saying why that side matters for the information in the threat.
note: A prompt per part of each code: E5-SYS-HW-12 (for each of the four operations in the traced task, the hardware part and the software doing it, named on the new diagram), E5-SYS-NT-14 (each part and its job, wired and wireless), E5-SYS-SE-13 (at least one threat per side; for each, the side and why that side matters for the information in the threat). No opening trace; the paper takes the session. Response time: day 5. Unplugged.

goal: Respond day: the paper's errors retaught by letter, and each missed item asked again in a new form.
note: Opens with the wrong example most of the class missed. Unit 2 needs no readiness check (its rows assume grade 4 rows, retrieved). Shorter year: fold-in day 2 (see the scope and sequence).

goal: Hook and the compelling question: a given flowchart for a step counter (start event, a repeated step, a count variable box, a decision diamond that reads it) is traced on a trace-table; then students change the goal in the decision and trace again, as grade 4's numbered sentences become boxes, diamonds and arrows.
note: Opens with the three-minute retrieval trace. Retrieval: trace a four-line written algorithm on a step-card (g4-written-algorithm), then the same steps become boxes. Math bridge (m5-two-patterns, math grade 5 unit 10 is weeks 27 to 30, later): the counter adds the same amount each time round, counting on that earlier grades' math gave; the trace-table lists the value each time round, no second pattern or graph. The step counter is about a toy or game, never a student's own body or fitness. Unplugged. Base: archived Year 6 Sensing movement lesson 5 (the step-counter design idea only, on paper; not yet loaded, later.csv L149).

goal: Pairs plan on a design sheet (player, rules, score, end), then draw a flowchart for a score game of their own with a start event, a repeat, a score variable and a decision on the score, trace it on a trace-table and check it against a partner's trace.
note: Opens with the three-minute retrieval trace. Retrieval: where the score variable is kept on the system-diagram. Index cards with branches or formal symbols, either; every control structure appears across one or more drawings. Math bridge as day 6. These games become unit 3's programs. Unplugged. Base: archived Year 6 Variables in games lesson 4 (designing a game; the design-sheet order is the Candidate kept at zero days), moved ahead of the code; not yet loaded (later.csv L149).

goal: Human-centered design in four ideas (ask who will use it, include different users, test with them, improve) and what a designer weighs (user needs, accessibility, fairness, the designer's own values), found or missed in a given library catalog search page; students fill a benefit-risk-chart on a choice there that was unfair for some users, then change one rule of their day 7 game for a player it leaves out.
note: Opens with the three-minute retrieval trace. Retrieval: who did one grade 4 rule help or leave out (g4-algorithm-groups). Sensitive: disability content (a user who cannot see the screen or use a mouse); talk is about what a design lets a person do, never about a classmate, in the wording the sensitivity read settles from its pack. Screenshots drawn by Curio Class, no product named. Unplugged.

goal: End-of-unit assessment, a written paper of about 25 minutes with unseen items: draw and trace a flowchart for a new task with an event, a repeat, a decision and a variable; for a new given technology, name two human-centered ideas it uses or misses and one change for a user it leaves out, with the reason.
note: A prompt per part: E5-ALG-PS-01 (each of event, repeat, decision and variable drawn, then traced), E5-ALG-IM-03 (two ideas named, one change with its reason). This record for E5-ALG-IM-03 is carried unscored into the mid-year check. No opening trace. Response time: day 10. Unplugged.

goal: Respond day: the paper's errors retaught by letter, each missed item asked again in a new form, and each pair's day 7 flowchart fixed where the paper showed a gap, ready to be unit 3's plan.
note: Opens with the wrong example most of the class missed. Week 10 is a core check week (science); a respond day is not a check day. Unit 3 needs no readiness check (grade 4 rows, retrieved). Shorter year: fold-in day 3.

goal: Hook and the compelling question: the class's score game adds a point but never says "you win"; students act as the computer with labeled paper cups as named boxes for a four-line program, then trace programs that store, compare and change a value (a score that goes up, a countdown that fires an event at zero, a typed guess compared with a pretend password) on a trace-table before running each step by step.
note: Opens with the three-minute retrieval trace. Retrieval: three-minute trace of a counter (g4-trace-values), and the unit 2 flowchart the game came from. "Set score to score plus 1" is said, never "score equals score plus 1": assignment is not equality. Unplugged cups first, then our own block editor with its text view and step-through trace, about 20 minutes. The pretend password is made up, never a real one. Paths: one device per pair; a few devices at stations with the other pairs on the paper version; one screen with a student at the keys for each step; no device. E5-PRO-VD-06 is part met without a device. Driver and navigator switch at the halfway signal. Devices carried with two hands, cords behind the table. Shorter year (fold 1): the day keeps the score program only; the countdown and password programs move into day 13's buggy set. Base: archived Year 6 Variables in games lesson 1 (not yet loaded, later.csv L149).

goal: Modify: change the compare value, the update or the start value of a working score game, predict what changes, run it and check, recording what was tested and what was changed.
note: Opens with the three-minute retrieval trace. Retrieval: where the score is held while the program runs (memory on the system-diagram). Device about 30 minutes, driver and navigator switching at the halfway signal. Paths: one device per pair; a few devices at stations with the other pairs on the paper version; one screen with a student at the keys for each step; no device. No-device path: printed program, paper cups, a partner acting as the computer. Devices carried with two hands, cords behind the table. Base: archived Year 6 Variables in games lesson 2 (not yet loaded). Shorter year: fold-in day 1.

goal: Debugging as a method: the teacher models two systematic strategies on given buggy programs, trace by hand and test one part at a time, and pairs try each in turn, recording on a test-table what was tested, expected, happened and the fix, then say which strategy found the bug and why.
note: Opens with the three-minute retrieval trace. Retrieval: which piece was added last (g4-debug-increment). Device about 25 minutes. Paths: one device per pair; a few devices at stations with the other pairs on the paper version; one screen with a student at the keys for each step; no device. No-device path: printed buggy programs and trace-tables. Shorter year (fold 1): the day 11 countdown and password programs join the buggy set. Driver and navigator switch at the halfway signal. Devices carried with two hands, cords behind the table.

goal: A third strategy, taking pieces out to isolate the bug, is modeled on one program; then on new buggy programs each pair chooses a strategy, uses a second on the next bug, fixes and retests, and compares which worked better, with each student's test-table holding two strategies, the fix, the retest and the line "what I tested and what I changed".
note: Opens with the three-minute retrieval trace. Retrieval: trace the day 6 step-counter flowchart. Kind: Understanding, not the frame's Fluency, because the day first shows the third strategy (GLOSSARY "teaching day"; For the lead 2). Reading the tool's message and a temporary output (a sound or a shown value) are short techniques used when a bug calls for them, not a checklist. The test-table is kept as evidence for the mid-year check, not scored today. Device about 30 minutes. Paths: one device per pair; a few devices at stations with the other pairs on the paper version; one screen with a student at the keys for each step; no device. Driver and navigator switch at the halfway signal. Devices carried with two hands, cords behind the table.

goal: Remix: a worked remix is traced first; then pairs modify a working game and combine it with a part of a teacher or peer program to make a new variation (a level, a timer, a new ending), crediting the source in a comment read in the text view.
note: Opens with the three-minute retrieval trace. Retrieval: which of two given programs is clearer, and why (g4-compare-solutions). Kind: the first day of E5-PRO-PD-04, so Understanding (GLOSSARY), though its second half is the make. Credit is taught as respect for another person's work. Device about 30 minutes. Paths: one device per pair; a few devices at stations with the other pairs on the paper version; one screen with a student at the keys for each step; no device. No-device path: cut and paste a printed program into a new one. Driver and navigator switch at the halfway signal. Devices carried with two hands, cords behind the table. Base: archived Year 6 Variables in games lesson 3 (improving a game, as the remix; not yet loaded).

goal: Team build: a worked component (a finished timer block with its inline comment and a three-line project note) is read in the text view and placed by following its note, about 6 minutes; then teams of three, roles named in advance, build the score game from a unit 2 flowchart, each student building one component (the score with a variable and a decision; the movement, given as a partly finished shell that its student modifies before making; the timer) and writing an inline comment and a short project note another student could use to put it in place.
note: Opens with the three-minute retrieval trace. Retrieval: read a comment and say what its part does (g4-team-document), and who the unit 2 game is for. Kind: first day of E5-PRO-PD-05 and E5-PRO-RD-07, so Understanding (GLOSSARY). Roles switch so no student holds the keys all session; a student with a motor or vision disability takes the navigator or tester role by choice, and the editor works by keyboard alone. Device about 30 minutes. Paths: one device per pair; a few devices at stations with the other pairs on the paper version; one screen with a student at the keys for each step; no device. No-device path: printed block strips cut and pasted into a team sheet, the tester acting as the computer. Devices carried with two hands, cords behind the table. Base: archived Year 6 Variables in games lesson 5 (design to code; not yet loaded).

goal: Team test: a student who did not write a component assembles and tests it, the test-table becoming the team's written feedback; the team fixes what it finds with the day 13 and 14 strategies, retests, and finishes the project note (purpose, parts, credits).
note: Opens with the three-minute retrieval trace. Retrieval: which side of the cia-triangle a changed component would hurt. The revised project is collected at the end of the session and scored here on the rubric with an individual record for each student (own component, its integration, its tests, its note: E5-PRO-PD-05, E5-PRO-RD-07), and carried into day 18's check, which is the unit's end-of-unit assessment. A student whose component does not set, update and compare a variable does a short supplied-shell modification today (E5-PRO-VD-06). Day 18 reuses this record and does not collect it again. The base's improve-and-share step (the Candidate) is folded into the test by a non-author, zero days. Device about 30 minutes. Paths: one device per pair; a few devices at stations with the other pairs on the paper version; one screen with a student at the keys for each step; no device. No-device path: printed block strips cut and pasted into a team sheet, the tester acting as the computer. Driver and navigator switch at the halfway signal. Devices carried with two hands, cords behind the table. Base: archived Year 6 Variables in games lesson 6 (not yet loaded).

goal: Mid-year course-level check, standing as unit 3's end-of-unit assessment: about 20 minutes written and unseen (trace a new score program that stores, compares and modifies a value, and predict its output; find and fix a bug in a new program with two named strategies, a test-table line each and the retest; three short new items on units 1 and 2) and about 10 minutes of device rotation (place one of three credited code segments, change one value, test, credit it, one line on what is new).
skills: g5-variables-use; g5-systematic-debug; g5-remix-program; g5-team-project; g5-visual-algorithm; g5-cia-triad; g5-hardware-software
codes: E5-PRO-VD-06; E5-PRO-TR-08; E5-PRO-PD-04; E5-PRO-PD-05; E5-PRO-RD-07; E5-ALG-PS-01; E5-SYS-SE-13; E5-SYS-HW-12
note: Week 18. This check is unit 3's end-of-unit assessment, so its unit 3 items are that unit's own unseen items; the unit 1 and 2 items (a new short flowchart traced, E5-ALG-PS-01; a new threat on the triangle, E5-SYS-SE-13; where a new task's data is stored, E5-SYS-HW-12) are new and differ in form from the day 4 and day 9 papers. E5-PRO-PD-05 and E5-PRO-RD-07 come from the day 17 record (reused, not collected again); the unseen trace item holds all three of store, compare and modify for E5-PRO-VD-06, beside that record's own set, update and compare; E5-ALG-IM-03's day 9 record is carried unscored. The debug item is individual on an unseen printed program, not day 17's team test. Device rotation 10 minutes covering both students of a pair; paper version cut and paste. Set-up 3, written 20, rotation 10, put-away 4. Devices carried with two hands, cords behind the table.

goal: Respond day for unit 3 and the check: errors retaught by letter and fresh evidence gathered on each missed item in a new form.
note: Week 19. Opens with the wrong example most of the class missed. Unit 4 needs no readiness check (grade 4 rows, retrieved). Device in part where a missed item is a device item, about 10 minutes; paper version of the missed device item. Devices carried with two hands, cords behind the table.

goal: Hook and the compelling question: a model trained on the class's first drawings calls every small triangle a circle (on the paper path, a printed result card of that model's wrong answers); then students collect data of two kinds with a tool (a pretend class survey on a form, the classroom thermometer's readings), organize it in a data-table, label each column numeric or descriptive, sort a numeric column and group the descriptive answers.
note: Opens with the three-minute retrieval trace. Retrieval: which is a row and which a column (g4-table-tool). Device about 30 minutes: a form and a table tool on the device. The survey is pretend (which of four indoor games, how many paper-airplane loops) and names no one; no prompt asks about a student's home, body, food, pets or family. Paths: one device per pair; a few devices at stations with the other pairs on the paper version; one screen with a student at the keys for each step; no device. No-device path: a paper form and a hand-sorted table; E5-DAT-DC-09 is part met without a device. Driver and navigator switch at the halfway signal. Devices carried with two hands, cords behind the table. Base: archived Year 6 Introduction to spreadsheets lessons 1 and 2 (collecting, then formatting: the Candidate order, kept at zero days; not yet loaded).

goal: Variability: a given dataset of repeated toy-car ramp times and the class's own three trials do not all match; students mark the typical values and the outlier on a dot chart, give possible sources of the difference and name one relationship between two columns (ramp height and time), with no statistic computed.
note: Opens with the three-minute retrieval trace. Retrieval: read one bar of a given chart (g4-data-explain). Science bridge (s5-design-test, science grade 5 unit 6 is weeks 25 to 30, later): the day teaches itself why one trial run several times gives different times; it plans no fair test and changes no variable. The ramp dataset is invented for practice. Ramp: a book-and-board slope on the floor; cars are not thrown. Unplugged, with the dataset sorted on the device in part, about 10 minutes. No device: the class sorts the printed ramp times by hand. Devices carried with two hands, cords behind the table.

goal: Training a model: the teacher trains a model on a supplied labeled set of shapes and tests it on a supplied test set while students predict which test drawings it gets right, check, change one training example and predict again; then pairs build their own labeled training-set of drawn shapes, train a small classifier and count how many of ten new drawings in a separate test set it gets right.
note: Opens with the three-minute retrieval trace. Retrieval: predict a sorter's output from a one-color training set (g4-ml-learning). Kind: first day of E5-ALG-ML-02, so Understanding, not the frame's Application (GLOSSARY; For the lead 2). The on-device trainer (later.csv L148) does not exist yet, so the day runs on the paper path: the model is a partner (or a card procedure) who may look only at the training cards and labels each test card with the label of the training card it matches most closely on stated features (size, number of corners, line thickness, tilt), never by knowing the shape, so a training set of only large, upright, thick-lined triangles mislabels small tilted ones; E5-ALG-ML-02 is part met until the trainer exists. When it exists: device about 25 minutes, drawings only, no camera or microphone, no drawing shows a person. Paths: one device per pair; a few devices at stations with the other pairs on the paper version; one screen with a student at the keys for each step; no device. Driver and navigator switch at the halfway signal. Devices carried with two hands, cords behind the table.

goal: Retrain: pairs look at which drawings are missing from their training-set (small, tilted, thin-lined shapes), add more varied examples, retrain and compare the before and after counts out of ten, and say why the training data changes what the model gets right.
note: Opens with the three-minute retrieval trace. Retrieval: a test-table line from unit 3 (the model's test counts are kept the same way). Each student's training choices, before and after counts and one-line explanation are the training record, scored here (the session after the row is first taught) and carried into day 25's check, which is the unit's end-of-unit assessment; day 25 reuses it and does not collect it again. Paper path until the trainer exists (later.csv L148): the student chooses the training cards to add and predicts, then the partner model relabels the test cards by closest match on the stated features and the before and after counts are compared; part met. When it exists: device about 30 minutes. Paths: one device per pair; a few devices at stations with the other pairs on the paper version; one screen with a student at the keys for each step; no device. Driver and navigator switch at the halfway signal. Devices carried with two hands, cords behind the table.

goal: Data benefits and risks: case cards of everyday technologies that use collected data (a weather forecast, a route planner, a step-count tracker, a recommendation list); students fill a benefit-risk-chart, name the cia-triangle side at risk, and give one limit that would make each safer.
note: Opens with the three-minute retrieval trace. Retrieval: name who collects one given dataset (g4-data-people), and the cia-triangle side, as review. Kind: first day of E5-DAT-IM-11, so Understanding (GLOSSARY). Case cards name no company and carry dated source lines; no student's own data or device is discussed. Unplugged.

goal: Year-end course-level check, standing as unit 4's end-of-unit assessment: about 12 minutes of device rotation (enter four fictional case cards through the form, then label, sort and group in the table tool) and about 18 minutes written and unseen (variability on a new dataset; a new data case answered in sentence frames; three short new items on units 1 to 3).
skills: g5-collect-tools; g5-variability; g5-data-benefits-risks; g5-train-model; g5-network-parts; g5-variables-use; g5-systematic-debug
codes: E5-DAT-DC-09; E5-DAT-DI-10; E5-DAT-IM-11; E5-ALG-ML-02; E5-SYS-NT-14; E5-PRO-VD-06; E5-PRO-TR-08
note: Week 25. A look-for per part: E5-DAT-DC-09 (entered, labeled, sorted, grouped; part met on the paper path, a paper form and hand-sorted table); E5-DAT-DI-10 (typical values and outlier marked, two sources, one relationship, each separate); E5-DAT-IM-11 (who gains, who is at risk and one limit, in two sentence frames, so the day 24 chart form is not repeated a week later); E5-ALG-ML-02 from the day 23 record (reused, not collected again). Units 1 to 3, about 6 of the 18 minutes: a wired or wireless part and its job (E5-SYS-NT-14), a variable's value after a short new program (E5-PRO-VD-06), the first wrong line in a new buggy program (E5-PRO-TR-08). Unit 3's project record stands as scored on day 17. Set-up 3, rotation 12, written 18, put-away 4. Answer-key agent read. Devices carried with two hands, cords behind the table.

goal: Respond day for unit 4 and the check: errors retaught by letter, missed items asked again in a new form, and each student's support and gains recorded for grade 6.
note: Week 26. Opens with the wrong example most of the class missed. Unit 5 needs no readiness check (grade 4 rows, retrieved).

goal: Hook and the compelling question: a sign-up form will not accept an invented name with a space and an accent mark; then two cases taught whole (the name form, captions made with Deaf users) and three by pair jigsaw (a voice tool that does not hear every accent, a keyboard for a language made with its speakers, an early programming language written in English-like words), each told by what happened with two views and a dated source, each pair placing one card on the timeline and reporting one line; students list who was included or left out, what it changed in how the tool was made, what it changed for the people who use it, and one change they would make.
note: Opens with the three-minute retrieval trace. Retrieval: place one grade 4 timeline card (g4-history-limits), and one design from unit 2 that left a player out. Sensitive: disability, language, naming and culture content. Names on cards are invented; no student's own name is tested on the form; the language keyboard case is replaced if its community's own account cannot be found, and a Native language case gets the full read for Native content first; the sensitivity agent reads the starting pack first. The programming language card's two views: it opened programming to people who were not mathematicians, and it was written in English words, which left out people who did not read English. No company named. Unplugged.

goal: How computing systems change culture and the ways people live and work, helping and hindering: how sharing short videos changed how families keep in touch and how news spreads, and how a translator's or an illustrator's job is changing as generative tools arrive, from a dated labor source; students place each change on the timeline with one help and one hindrance.
note: Opens with the three-minute retrieval trace. Retrieval: one way a widely used system affects resources (g4-resources). Sensitive: work and automation can touch a family; no student is asked about a family member's job, and a student's own offer is welcome. Teacher source line: the US Bureau of Labor Statistics Occupational Outlook Handbook pages Interpreters and Translators (modified 2026-08-27: the new tools make the work more efficient, and many jobs cannot be fully automated) and Craft and Fine Artists (modified 2026-10-29: machine-made illustrations may compete with illustrators), the two views of the case. Students do not use social media or generative tools. Unplugged. Base: archived Year 6 Communication and collaboration lesson 5 (not yet loaded, later.csv L149).

goal: When to use computing: from case cards (counting votes in a class election, translating a short sign, choosing who gets the last turn, comforting a friend) students fill a benefit-risk-chart and answer "should a person decide this?"; then why a pictured family might choose to use or not use a new home device (cost, privacy, who in the family can use it), without saying whether a choice is right.
note: Opens with the three-minute retrieval trace. Retrieval: predict a sorter's output (g4-ml-learning), and a grade 4 limit of an existing technology (g4-history-limits), beside unit 4's model that was wrong for some shapes. The family case is a pictured family, never a student's own home; no judgment of a family's choice. Each claim carries two views and a dated source in the teacher line. Unplugged.

goal: Professionals working together with shared digital tools (a wildfire team of firefighters, weather scientists and mapmakers on one live map; a museum exhibit team of an artist, a historian and a programmer on one shared plan), then a short role-play of a class tool's team (designer, programmer, tester, user): what each adds and what goes wrong when one is missing.
note: Opens with the three-minute retrieval trace. Retrieval: what one grade 4 worker had to learn (g4-work-tools), and the unit 3 team roles. Unplugged. Base: archived Year 6 Communication and collaboration lessons 3 and 4 (not yet loaded, later.csv L149). The Candidate interview with a school worker is dropped (zero days; a visit needs the school's own arrangement).

goal: End-of-unit assessment, a written paper of about 25 minutes on new cases: who was included or left out, what it changed in how the tool was made and what it changed for the people who use it; one way a new system changes culture or how people live, and one way it changes work, each a help or a hindrance; two things a new family weighs about a new device; whether a new problem needs computing, decided and justified; how two new professionals share their work with a digital tool.
note: Week 31 (a math core check week; this is a unit assessment, not a course-level check). One prompt per code, each a short claim with a reason on a new case, never recognition of a supplied one. No opening trace. Response time: day 32. Unplugged.

goal: Respond day: the paper's errors retaught by letter, each missed item asked again on a new case, and the year closed with the compelling question answered from the year's own work.
note: Week 32. Opens with the wrong example most of the class missed. Unplugged.
